chapter: Cee Pee Johnson, Hampton and the Navy band
title: Personnel of the original Hampton band
summary: Fred Beckett, Ray Perry, Dexter Gordon, Illinois Jacquet, Ernie Royal, Milt Buckner and Vernon Alley among members.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who all else was in that band?
You mentioned about half the (inaudible) band. Who else was there besides (inaudible)?

Had a great trombone player by the name of Fred Beckett (PHONETIC). He was one of the smoothest, cleanest trombonists that you'd ever hear in life. We used to call him Black Dorsey. He could -- a very sensuous type of player, just a gorgeous player. He died at an early age with tuberculosis. We had Ray Perry that played electric violin, who was probably one of the best jazz violinists that ever was. He died at an early age. Then Dexter Gordon was in the

band, tenor saxophone player, Illinois Jacquet. Jack MacVeigh was baritone saxophone player, and I. Then Ernie Royal, trumpet player, and Carl George was there for a while and Joe Newman and they had another fellow who used to play a plunger, like the old Sam Nanton (PHONETIC) player with Ellington. We called him "Mushmouth." It was Sonny Craven (PHONETIC).

His nickname was "Mushmouth." Milt Buckner (PHONETIC) ended up being the regular pianist with the Hampton band, after Sir Charles Thompson (PHONETIC), who was the first beginner. We had a fellow by the name of Vernon Alley (bass) who was a staunch San Franciscoan. He came out of San Francisco for the first and only time in his life with that band and rushed right back home and immediately stayed there for the rest of his life, which he's still living. Of course, he was with our Navy band, of which I was the leader, during World War II at St. Mary's Pre-Flight School.
